recommendation: Keep the external-repo audit commit. If sparse differential handling still fails, reproduce and fix it in HL7/fhir-ig-publisher; no core FHIR specification edit is indicated by the current evidence.
issue_request: FHIR-14953 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core change request, raised in STU3 and applied for R5, asking that the IG Publisher work with sparse differentials instead of requiring parent nodes and the root element in every StructureDefinition differential.
initial_application: No current FHIR core source commit explicitly mentions FHIR-14953. The relevant core rule was already applied through FHIR-8971, including git commit b2cbcf3afa7ef4fd2dc92fb9da59eb8ed8894f1a, which documented that sparse differentials may omit the root element.
additional_context: Current source/profiling.html states that differential profiles can be sparse, mention only changed elements, and omit the root; source/hierarchy.xml includes profiling.html in the built Conformance module. Later Zulip and HL7/fhir-ig-publisher#111 evidence tracked a concrete snapshot-generation failure in IG Publisher tooling, and that GitHub issue was closed after the reporter confirmed it appeared resolved. Confluence searches found no conflicting or separate work-group evidence.
reconciliation: No core source files were changed. The core specification already conveys the sparse differential rule, and the requested behavior belongs to the external HL7/fhir-ig-publisher repository rather than this FHIR source checkout.
